title: Supplementary material, diadochokinetic tasks from childhood to adulthood
citation: Lancheros, M., Friedrichs, D. & Laganaro, M. What do differences between alternating and sequential diadochokinetic tasks tell us about the development of oromotor skills? 2023.

population.description: Participants across childhood, adolescence and adulthood; counts are not stated on the record.
limitations: The deposit contains derived measurements only. There is no audio.

failure_reasons: Without audio there is nothing for a candidate implementation to be run against, so this cannot serve as a reference for any computational or analytical validation.
Published summary values from another protocol are not a reference range for a different task, population or capture path.

findings: One spreadsheet of syllabic rate and articulatory execution measures for alternating and sequential tasks.
Open access under CC BY 4.0 with a single file and no recordings.

reasons: Openly licensed and freely obtainable, and still not a reference source, because it holds numbers rather than speech.
